discovery: Dynamical symmetries and supersymmetry in atomic nuclei: the interacting boson model and its experimental confirmation
motivation: Francesco Iachello (with the late Akito Arima) created the interacting boson model, showing that the collective spectra of complex nuclei are organised by the dynamical symmetries U(5), SU(3) and O(6). Iachello then predicted that bosonic even-even and fermionic odd nuclei can be unified within a single supergroup. This was the first physical realisation of supersymmetry and was confirmed as a dynamical symmetry of nature. Jan Jolie led the high-resolution spectroscopy, culminating in the 1999 identification of the 196Au supersymmetric partner in the Pt-Au quartet, which gave a decisive test of these predictions. Together these works turned group theory into a predictive language for many-body quantum systems. They explained shape phase transitions and critical-point symmetries, and they inspired algebraic methods across molecular, hadronic and mesoscopic physics. This is an elegant unification that has been confirmed by experiment.
